prompt: Create ONE standalone botanical illustration for The Vegetable Guru inner pages, not a page layout. The FIRST reference is a real photograph: use it for the vegetable shapes, asymmetry, angles, overlap and natural composition. References 2 and 3 are APPROVED BOOK HERO ART and must govern drawing style: bold simplified silhouettes, broad crisp colour and shadow planes, dimensional hand-shaped vector-like botanical drawing, rich natural crop colours, lime and forest greens, tapered cream highlight slashes and occasional rhythmic scalloped highlights, a few major veins only. No fine ink hatching, no watercolour, no pencil, no grain or mottled texture, no photographic skin gloss, no black outline. Ignore and DO NOT reproduce the reference heroes' green/black background haze. Genuinely transparent PNG background, no glow, no halo, no cast shadow or ground plane, no white backing, no lettering or border. Keep the entire silhouette inside the canvas with 7% clear padding. Large high resolution. Square. From the photo isolate a single rhubarb crown with FIVE thick pink/red-green stalks spreading in unequal directions and their large irregular broad leaves, the closest leaf leaning down-left. Retain the natural criss-crossing stalks and plant form; do not make a tidy fan of harvested sticks. Simplify the crowded scene to this connected crown, omit neighbours, weeds, flowers and soil. Make the fleshy stalks clearly visible. A handful of bold veins per leaf, not a dense etched network.
